name: Hathruna
known_status: One of the twenty-two imprisoned gods of Universal. Able to influence worshippers through sanctioned rites, dreams, omens, miracles, cults, and the institutions that maintain the divine prisons.
manifestation: Hathruna’s skin blooms with fungal growths that open and close like breathing flowers.
deity_description: In Universal, the ancient gods are not distant myths but imprisoned systems of appetite and control, bound within metaphysical vault-prisons forged four centuries ago by an unprecedented alliance of industrial powers, arcane orders, monarchies, and revolutionary movements. The Universalian pantheon once ruled openly across the continent, sustained not only by worship but by the extraction of mortal essence through prayer, sacrifice, emotion, and suffering. Valkhamesh governed storm and law from celestial courts, Horundar ruled the depths, Nefarokir presided over the dead, Raeshkul shaped strategy and empire, Enkirael fed upon war, and every other deity embodied a distinct form of consumption. Civilizations eventually learned that divinity was not symbolic but predatory, and that faith itself was a resource being harvested. This realization led to the construction of twenty-one seal-prisons designed not to kill the gods but to restrict their ability to feed, forcing them into controlled starvation while still allowing limited, regulated influence over mortal civilization. Even in containment, the gods remain active, whispering through dreams, sanctioned rituals, and tightly controlled divine systems that modern infrastructure still depends upon, from skyship arcane cores to portal stabilizers and consecrated rail wards. Beneath all of it lies the greater terror of Thoryn-Rahek, the first devourer, imprisoned deeper than the rest, whose eventual release is foretold to collapse the fragile balance between survival and annihilation.

Within this constrained divine ecology, Hathruna occupies one of the most essential and paradoxical thrones. She is not merely the goddess of seasonal change, but the structured axis between growth and consumption, life and refinement, ascent and descent. Born of Ishtanora and Valkhamesh, she was once seen as unclaimed fertility, though in Universalian theology this state is not innocence but unallocated potential within a predatory hierarchy. Her descent into the Underworld is not treated as abduction alone, but as ritual acquisition, the moment she is integrated into the chthonic economy governed alongside Nefarokir. The meadow of flowers where she transitions between worlds is understood as a threshold site where mortal vitality becomes negotiable substance. The pomegranate she consumes is not a symbolic fruit but a sealed vessel of condensed life essence, each seed binding her to the cyclical obligation of regulated harvest and return. Through this act, she becomes both sovereign and instrument, ensuring that divine consumption does not collapse into chaos but remains structured as rhythm, a controlled alternation between abundance and depletion that stabilizes the entire metaphysical order.

In the modern Age of Containment, Hathruna’s role has become even more critical, as the sealed gods continue to hunger beneath their prisons while mortal civilization relies upon carefully regulated divine extraction to sustain its infrastructure. She functions as a stabilizing intermediary between Ishtanora’s surface domain of managed abundance and Nefarokir’ subterranean administration of consumed essence, ensuring that neither unchecked growth nor uncontrolled depletion destabilizes the cycle. Even imprisoned gods acknowledge her as one of the few forces capable of maintaining continuity within a collapsing divine ecosystem. Where other deities lash out against their confinement or whisper rebellion through fractured worship, Hathruna enforces structure upon the process itself, embodying the principle that survival in Universal is not the absence of consumption, but its regulation into form.
public_lore: Hathruna governs decay as preparation for new life: fungi, roots, compost, seasonal death, regrowth, and wilderness that feeds on its own remains. Her followers regard rot not as corruption but as transformation and return.
common_worship: Honored by gardeners, herbalists, composters, mushroom cultivators, undertakers, and forest communities.
religious_warning: Hathruna’s renewal rarely preserves the previous form. Rebirth may continue a cycle while ending the individual who entered it.
public_origin_record: No reliable mortal record explains what this being was before the age of divine rule. Temple accounts, forbidden histories, and prison records contradict one another.

pantheon_source.document_summary: A narrative pantheon compendium preserving each deity’s domains, manifestation, divine character, and sacred history.

canon_authority.authority_rule: The canonical 22-god order and dedicated creator compendium govern every deity-to-people relationship; province and settlement placement does not alter divine parentage or race canon.

created_races.family_description: Plantfolk and Nature-Bound Races contains the canonical parent races Mandrake, Mycelian, Gnarlborn, and Harvestborn. No additional canonical bloodline, lineage, or non-bloodline form menu is assigned to this category. All of these ancestries remain under Hathruna's single creator category.
created_races.creation_doctrine: Canonical race-compendium doctrine: Hathruna holds this single creator category through seasonal rebirth, decay, fungi, roots, plant life, compost, and living wilderness. The canonical parent races are Mandrake, Mycelian, Gnarlborn, and Harvestborn. No additional canonical bloodline, lineage, or non-bloodline form menu is assigned to this category. Temple language preserves reverence, but its colder margins classify each race, bloodline, lineage, and form by yield, pressure, environment, devotion, fear, beauty, endurance, and the particular note it awakens in the god's appetite.
created_races.created_peoples_record: Hathruna is recorded as the single creator-god of the Plantfolk and Nature-Bound Races category: Mandrake, Mycelian, Gnarlborn, and Harvestborn. No additional canonical bloodline, lineage, or non-bloodline form menu is assigned to this category. The public hymn calls this lineage and blessing; the older register reads like curated divine husbandry, sorting bodies, habitats, temperaments, and spirit-resonance so seasonal rebirth, decay, fungi, roots, plant life, compost, and living wilderness never depends on one mortal pattern alone.

parent_races.name: Mandrake
parent_races.description: Plantfolk born from uprooted magical mandrake roots that retain faint echoes of ancient curses. Their cries can be dangerous, but they are deeply protective of sacred soil and growth. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

parent_races.name: Mycelian
parent_races.description: Fungal humanoids connected through vast underground mycelial networks that share memory and sensation. They act as living archives of forest knowledge and decay cycles. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

parent_races.name: Gnarlborn
parent_races.description: Woody, bark-skinned beings shaped from ancient trees that gained sentience through centuries of druidic influence. They are slow-moving but possess immense endurance and natural resilience. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

parent_races.name: Harvestborn
parent_races.description: Seasonal plantfolk tied to cycles of growth and decay, often blooming with crops, grain, or fruit-like features. They are communal caretakers who embody abundance, sacrifice, and renewal. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.
